info.name: FML R4-R6 FHIR server
info.description:
Tries out BodyStructure through /R4 and /R6 on the same stored R4 data.

**Before you start:** `git submodule update --init --recursive`, `bun install`, `bun run build:fml`, `bun run db:up`, then `bun run dev`. The server listens on `http://localhost:8080`; change the `baseUrl` collection variable if yours differs.

**How to run:** use Run collection to go top to bottom, or send requests by hand in order, because later requests use the id and rows saved by earlier ones. Run folder 2 again for a fresh resource; folder 7 deletes it.

Diagrams of the mapping are in `docs/mappings.html`.

item.name: 1. Check the server
item.description: Run this first. If it fails, start the database and server (see the collection description).

item.name: R4 capability statement
R6 capability statement

exec: pm.test("BodyStructure can be written", () => pm.expect(resources.find(r => r.type === "BodyStructure").interaction.map(i => i.code)).to.include("create"));
pm.test("Patient can be written", () => pm.expect(resources.find(r => r.type === "Patient").interaction.map(i => i.code)).to.include.members(["create", "update", "delete"]));

item.name: 2. One R6 resource becomes three R4 rows
item.description: The main case. One R6 BodyStructure with three includedStructure entries is stored as rows <id>, <id>--2 and <id>--3.

item.name: Create through R6 (3 structures)

exec: pm.test("structures are Forearm, Upper arm, Shoulder", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure.map(i => i.structure.text)).to.eql(["Forearm", "Upper arm", "Shoulder"]));

request.description: Saves the new id as {{bsId}} and the ETag for later requests.

item.name: Read through R6: one resource

exec: pm.test("structures are Forearm, Upper arm, Shoulder", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure.map(i => i.structure.text)).to.eql(["Forearm", "Upper arm", "Shoulder"]));
pm.test("laterality is back in its own field", () => pm.expect(first.laterality.text).to.eql("Left"));
pm.test("qualifier has only Volar", () => pm.expect(first.qualifier.map(q => q.text)).to.eql(["Volar"]));

item.name: Read through R4: primary row

exec: pm.test("first morphology is on the element", () => pm.expect(row.morphology.text).to.eql("Basal cell carcinoma"));
pm.test("second morphology is in an extension", () => pm.expect(row.extension[0].valueCodeableConcept.text).to.eql("Nevus sebaceus"));
pm.test("laterality and qualifier share locationQualifier", () => pm.expect(row.locationQualifier.map(q => q.text)).to.eql(["Volar", "Left"]));

pm.test("lists the other rows", () => { const link = row.extension.find(e => e.url.endsWith("bodystructure-row-group")); const id = pm.collectionVariables.get("bsId"); pm.expect(link.extension.filter(e => e.url === "member").map(e => e.valueReference.reference)).to.eql(["BodyStructure/" + id + "--2", "BodyStructure/" + id + "--3"]); });

item.name: Read through R4: row 2
Read through R4: row 3
3. Edit through R4, read through R6
item.description: The same data, used through both versions. Run in order after folder 2.

item.name: Get row 2 to edit
Change location on row 2 through R4
Read through R6: only structure 2 changed

exec: pm.test("structures are Forearm, Elbow, Shoulder", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure.map(i => i.structure.text)).to.eql(["Forearm", "Elbow", "Shoulder"]));

item.name: R6 update with the old ETag is refused

request.description: The R4 edit moved the version, so this stale write must not overwrite anything.

item.name: Get row 3 to edit
Change description on row 3 through R4

request.description: description is shared, so it must reach every row and the R6 view.

item.name: Read through R6: description changed

exec: pm.test("shows the new description", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().description).to.eql("Edited on row 3 through R4"));

item.name: Read primary row: description changed too

exec: pm.test("shows the new description", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().description).to.eql("Edited on row 3 through R4"));

item.name: R4 client sends the row without our extensions

exec: pm.test("the server restored the extra morphology", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().extension.some(e => e.valueCodeableConcept && e.valueCodeableConcept.text === "Nevus sebaceus")).to.be.true);

request.description: A typical R4 client drops extensions it doesn't understand. R6-only data must survive.

item.name: Read through R6: laterality and morphology survived

exec: pm.test("both morphology values are still there", () => pm.expect(first.morphology.length).to.eql(2));

item.name: Get primary row again
Remove the laterality code through R4
Read through R6: laterality is gone
4. Requests that must be rejected
item.description: Each of these stores nothing. Folder 4 needs {{bsId}} from folder 2 only for the row id check.

item.name: R6 without patient (valid R6, not storable as R4)
R6 with modifierExtension (can't be understood safely)
Extension using a URL the mapping relies on
R6 Patient with contact.role (R6 only, not storable as R4)
R6-only extension type has no R4 form

request.description: Every write is converted and converted back. Anything that doesn't survive returns 422.

item.name: R6 with contained resources (no R4 place)
R6 attachment too large for R4

request.description: R6 size is integer64, but R4 size is unsignedInt.

item.name: R4 without location (valid R4, not readable as R6)
R4 row ids don't exist in R6
New ids can't contain the reserved --
5. Real HL7 examples and every element
item.description: R6 examples with one includedStructure become one R4 row. Landmarks and every other element survive in extensions.

item.name: Create tumor example through R6
Read tumor through R4: one row

exec: pm.test("morphology comes from the structure", () => pm.expect(row.morphology.text).to.eql("Splenic mass"));

item.name: No second row exists
Create fetus example through R6
Create skin-patch example through R6 (has landmarks)
Read skin-patch through R4: landmarks are in an extension
Read skin-patch through R6: landmarks are back
Create with every element through R6

exec: pm.test("structures are Forearm, Upper arm", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure.map(i => i.structure.text)).to.eql(["Forearm", "Upper arm"]));

item.name: Excluded structure never becomes a row

request.description: Only the two included structures have rows. The excluded one is an extension.

item.name: Read through R6: nothing was lost

exec: pm.test("size is an R6 string again", () => pm.expect(r.includedStructure[0].image[0].size).to.eql("1234"));

item.name: 6. Created through R4, extended through R6
item.description: The other direction: a plain R4 resource grows a second structure through R6.

item.name: Create through R4
Read through R6: one structure
Add a structure through R6
Read through R4: original row intact

exec: pm.test("still Spleen with its morphology", () => { const r = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(r.location.text).to.eql("Spleen"); pm.expect(r.morphology.text).to.eql("Mass"); });

item.name: Read through R4: new row
7. Stable row ids and links
item.description: A row keeps its id while its structure exists, and numbers are never reused.

item.name: Create through R6 (3 structures)
Row 3 shows its link

exec: pm.test("points at the primary row", () => pm.expect(link.extension.find(e => e.url === "primary").valueReference.reference).to.eql("BodyStructure/" + pm.collectionVariables.get("stableId")));

item.name: Delete row 2 through R4
Read through R6: row 3 kept its id
Add a structure through R6: gets a new number

exec: pm.test("structures are Forearm, Shoulder, Neck", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure.map(i => i.structure.text)).to.eql(["Forearm", "Shoulder", "Neck"]));

item.name: Deleted number stays deleted
Reorder through R6: row ids don't change

exec: pm.test("structures are Neck, Shoulder, Forearm", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure.map(i => i.structure.text)).to.eql(["Neck", "Shoulder", "Forearm"]));

item.name: Primary row still holds its structure
Remove the primary row's structure through R6

request.description: The one exception: the R6 resource needs a row with its own id, so the first remaining structure moves into the primary row.

item.name: Primary row now holds the next structure

exec: pm.test("lists the one remaining row", () => { const link = pm.response.json().extension.find(e => e.url.endsWith("bodystructure-row-group")); const id = pm.collectionVariables.get("stableId"); pm.expect(link.extension.filter(e => e.url === "member").map(e => e.valueReference.reference)).to.eql(["BodyStructure/" + id + "--3"]); });

item.name: Its old row is gone
8. Removing extensions through R4
item.description: A client that drops extensions keeps them; a client can still remove one on purpose.

item.name: Create with an extra morphology
Read the R4 row
PUT without extensions: they come back
Read through R6: extra is still there

exec: pm.test("morphology is Basal cell carcinoma, Nevus sebaceus", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure[0].morphology.map(m => m.text)).to.eql(["Basal cell carcinoma", "Nevus sebaceus"]));

item.name: Same PUT with X-Replace-Extensions: removed
Read through R6: extra is gone

exec: pm.test("morphology is Basal cell carcinoma", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().includedStructure[0].morphology.map(m => m.text)).to.eql(["Basal cell carcinoma"]));

item.name: 8b. Your own extensions and attachment language
item.description: Extensions we don't recognise are carried across. One on the resource is on every row; one on a structure stays on its row.

item.name: Create with extensions and attachment language
Read through R6: everything is where it was sent

exec: pm.test("structure extension is on structure 2 only", () => { pm.expect(r.includedStructure[1].extension[0].valueBoolean).to.eql(true); pm.expect(r.includedStructure[0].extension).to.be.undefined; });

item.name: Read row 2 through R4: both are there

exec: pm.test("has the wrapped resource extension", () => pm.expect(urls.some(u => u.endsWith("extension-BodyStructure.extension"))).to.be.true);

item.name: 8c. Patient and Encounter through R6
item.description: Stored as one R4 resource each. R6 reads run the R4 -> R6 maps; R6 writes run the R6 -> R4 maps and are stored only if they convert back unchanged.

item.name: Create a Patient through R4
Read it through R6
Create an Encounter through R4
Read it through R6: class is a list, finished is completed
Update the Encounter through R6: add a second class
Read it through R4: the second class is an extension

exec: pm.test("R6 completed is R4 finished", () => pm.expect(e.status).to.eql("finished"));
pm.test("class is the first class", () => pm.expect(e.class.code).to.eql("AMB"));

pm.test("the second class is an extension", () => pm.expect(e.extension.find(x => x.url === "http://hl7.org/fhir/6.0/StructureDefinition/extension-Encounter.class").valueCodeableConcept.coding[0].code).to.eql("VR"));

item.name: Create a Patient through R6
Read it through R4: R6-only photo height is an extension
Delete it through R6
8d. Observation references to a split BodyStructure
item.description: In R4 the reference is the standard bodySite extension on Observation.bodySite, and can point at one row. In R6 it is Observation.bodyStructure and always points at the whole resource.

item.name: Create a BodyStructure with three structures through R6
Create an Observation through R4, referencing row 2

exec: pm.test("the row reference is stored as sent", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().bodySite.extension[0].valueReference.reference).to.eql("BodyStructure/" + pm.collectionVariables.get("refBsId") + "--2"));

item.name: Read it through R6: bodyStructure is the whole resource

exec: pm.test("bodyStructure references the R6 resource", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().bodyStructure).to.eql([{ reference: { reference: "BodyStructure/" + pm.collectionVariables.get("refBsId") } }]));
pm.test("the extension isn't left on bodySite", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().bodySite).to.eql({ text: "arm" }));

item.name: Follow the R6 reference: all three structures

exec: pm.test("structures are Forearm, Upper arm, Shoulder", () => pm.expect(body.includedStructure.map(i => i.structure.text)).to.eql(["Forearm", "Upper arm", "Shoulder"]));

item.name: Remove the first structure through R6: row 2 moves into the primary row
Read the Observation through R4: the reference moved with it

exec: pm.test("now references the primary row", () => pm.expect(body.bodySite.extension[0].valueReference.reference).to.eql("BodyStructure/" + pm.collectionVariables.get("refBsId")));
pm.test("the change is a new version", () => pm.expect(body.meta.versionId).to.eql("2"));

item.name: Follow the R4 reference: the same structure
The old row returns 410
A bodySite reference to another type returns 422
A version-specific bodySite reference returns 422
8e. Observation CRUD through R6
item.description: Runs after 8d, which creates the BodyStructure {{refBsId}} and the Observation {{observationId}}. Every write must be valid in both versions.

item.name: Create through R6, referencing the whole BodyStructure

exec: pm.test("the R6-only element comes back", () => pm.expect(body.statusReason.text).to.eql("Sensor replaced"));

item.name: Read it through R4: stored as extensions

exec: pm.test("the reference is a bodySite extension", () => pm.expect(body.bodySite.extension[0]).to.eql({ url: "http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/bodySite", valueReference: { reference: "BodyStructure/" + pm.collectionVariables.get("refBsId") } }));

item.name: Read it through R6
Update through R6

bodyStructure.concept returns 422
